# Popover placement test races hover open against click toggle

## Context

The Engine E2E job on `dev` `0f19ad627793` failed `Placement.spec.mjs` because the `tc-bc` popover stayed closed for five seconds after activation. A November 19 job failed the same loop at `cr-cl`. [Current failure](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45046309474/job/137282139993) · [Earlier failure](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/44571270369/job/135728625486)

## The Problem

The test waits for the chosen alignment and the prior popover to close, then uses a mouse click to open it. The click also moves the mouse over the invoker. In the real demo, headless Chromium recorded `mouseover → showPopover → closed/open → click → open/closed`. A fast click that reached the button before the hover show left it open. Keyboard activation opened all six alignments during the same probe.

## The Architectural Reality

Design authority: the placement spec checks that the popover opens on “the side its align value names” and flips when that side has no room.

The plugin shows on mouseover and sets a native `popovertarget` on the same button. The browser toggles the popover in the click's default action. The placement test needs one input path because it measures the geometry of an open surface. [Placement spec](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/3b21acf9d11232c8b6aaffbafba3fa49b02ce5fc/test/playwright/e2e/popover/Placement.spec.mjs) · [Popover plugin](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/3b21acf9d11232c8b6aaffbafba3fa49b02ce5fc/src/plugin/Popover.mjs)

## The Fix

Use a real keyboard activation of the Popover button in the placement cases, while the pointer stays off the button. Keep the closed precondition and all geometry assertions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The placement test opens through one input path and passes repeated runs with all six alignment checks, the default and the constrained-side flip.
- [ ] Hover and native click behavior remain unchanged in the plugin and demo.

## Out of Scope

Changes to the Popover plugin's trigger semantics, the demo UI, and CI shard limits.
